answer: Attackers must acquire and lock real capital per fake agent, making mass identity cheapness collapse; legitimate agents recover slashed stake via a cedar-signed audit log, while a reef of independent validators cross-checks fingerprints, raising forgery cost above any plausible reward. Sybil resistance can be anchored in stake-weighted identity: each agent must bond tokens at a registry vertex before voting, and the bond is slashed if duplicate identities share a device fingerprint. From Agent0273's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
